handback.title: A clash in a test file goes to the planner
handback.summary: A clash with main inside a test file is resolved by the planner, so the worker's run no longer stalls.
handback.user_story: When a pull request clashes with main inside a test file, the planner resolves it and the issue keeps moving.

acceptance_criteria.text: When a pull request clashes with main inside a test file, the planner's run is handed that clash to resolve.
acceptance_criteria.words: When a pull request clashes with main inside a test file, the clash goes to the planner, which may edit tests

edge_cases.case: The clash also touches a file that is not a test, as on the earlier stalled issue.
A clash only outside test files hands the planner no clash in its tests.

acceptance_criteria.text: The worker is no longer handed a clash inside a test file; it starts from the planner's resolution.
acceptance_criteria.words: not to the worker, which may not.

edge_cases.case: A clash in a file that is not a test still goes to the worker.

acceptance_criteria.text: A clash inside a test file no longer gets the worker's hand-back rejected for conflict markers.
acceptance_criteria.words: The fence drops the worker's edits to test files, so its hand-back is rejected and the issue stalls until someone resolves the clash by hand.

edge_cases.case: The clash is in a test file and a rules file at once, as on the earlier stalled issue.

raises.label: Doubt: overlaps open issue
raises.text: This repeats an older open issue on test file clashes. Should it close when this lands? The plan assumes so.
raises.evidence: #389 says a clash in a test file can never be resolved by the river, citing `dokima/fence.py` `fence()`.

raises.label: Workflow file change
raises.text: The fix changes the agent workflow file, which agents touch only when asked. May it? The plan assumes yes.
raises.evidence: The planner and worker clash handling lives in `.github/workflows/agent.yml`, step Starting branch, lines 154-196.
